source_text: Fieri autem petimus uoluntatem Dei in caelo et in terra: quod utrumque ad consummationem nostrae incolumitatis pertinet et salutis. nam cum corpus e terra et spiritum possideamus e caelo, ipsi terra et caelum sumus et in utroque id est et corpore et spiritu ut Dei uoluntas fiat oramus. est enim inter carnem et spiritum conluctatio et discordantibus aduersum se inuicem cottidiana congressio, ut non quae uolumus ipsa faciamus, dum spiritus caelestia et diuina quaerit, caro terrena et saecularia concupiscit. et ideo petimus inter duo ista ope et auxilio Dei concordiam fieri, ut dum et in spiritu et in carne uoluntas Dei geritur, quae per eum renata est anima seruetur. quod aperte adque manifeste apostolus Paulus sua uoce declarat, caro, inquit, concupiscit aduersus spiritum et spiritus aduersus carnem haec enim inuicem aduersantur sibi, ut non quae uultis ipsa faciatis. manifesta autem sunt facta carnis quae sunt adulteria, fornicationes, inmunditiae, spurcitiae, idololatriae, ueneficia, homicidia, inimicitiae, contentiones, aemulationes, animositates, prouocationes, simultates, dissensiones, haereses, inuidiae, ebrietates, comisationes et his similia: qui talia agunt regnum Dei non possidebunt. fructus autem spiritus est caritas, gaudium, pax, magnanimitas, bonitas, fides, mansuetudo, continentia, castitas. et idcirco cottidianis immo continuis orationibus hoc precamur et in caelo et in terra uoluntatem circa nos Dei fieri: quia haec est uoluntas Dei ut terrena caelestibus cedant, spiritalia et diuina praeualeant.
thought_title: The conflict of flesh and spirit and the prayer for God's will in both
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'your will be done on earth as in heaven' by applying it to the believer's own body and spirit.
pass_a_gloss: But we ask that God's will be done in heaven and on earth: each of these two pertains to the completion of our safety and salvation. For since we possess a body from the earth and a spirit from heaven, we ourselves are earth and heaven, and in each, that is both in body and in spirit, we pray that God's will be done. For there is a struggle between flesh and spirit, and a daily conflict between them as they disagree against each other, so that we do not do the very things we wish, while the spirit seeks heavenly and divine things, the flesh desires earthly and worldly things. And therefore we ask that between these two, by the help and aid of God, concord be made, so that while God's will is carried out both in spirit and in flesh, the soul which has been reborn through him may be preserved. The apostle Paul declares this openly and clearly in his own voice: 'The flesh,' he says, 'lusts against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh; for these are opposed to each other, so that you do not do the very things you wish.' But the works of the flesh are manifest, which are adulteries, fornications, impurities, filthiness, idolatries, sorceries, murders, enmities, contentions, rivalries, animosities, provocations, quarrels, dissensions, heresies, envies, drunkennesses, revelings and things similar to these: those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, magnanimity, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control, chastity. And therefore by daily, indeed by continuous prayers we pray for this, that God's will be done around us both in heaven and on earth: because this is God's will, that earthly things yield to heavenly things, and spiritual and divine things prevail.

pass_b_english: We ask that God's will be done in heaven and on earth, and both of these concern the completion of our safety and salvation. For since we possess a body from the earth and a spirit from heaven, we ourselves are earth and heaven, and we pray that God's will be done in both—that is, in body and in spirit. There is a struggle between flesh and spirit, a daily conflict between them as they oppose each other, so that we do not do the very things we want: the spirit seeks heavenly and divine things, while the flesh desires earthly and worldly things. And so we ask that by God's help and aid concord be made between these two, so that while God's will is carried out in both spirit and flesh, the soul that has been reborn through him may be preserved. The apostle Paul declares this openly and clearly in his own voice: "The flesh desires against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh; for these are opposed to each other, so that you do not do the very things you want" (Galatians 5:17). "Now the works of the flesh are evident: adultery, fornication, impurity, filthiness, idolatry, sorcery, murders, enmities, contentions, rivalries, outbursts of anger, provocations, quarrels, dissensions, heresies, envy, drunkenness, carousing, and things like these. Those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God" (Galatians 5:19-21). "But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, magnanimity, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control, chastity" (Galatians 5:22-23). And therefore by daily, indeed by continuous prayers, we ask this: that God's will be done in heaven and on earth concerning us. For this is God's will: that earthly things yield to heavenly things, and spiritual and divine things prevail.

last_rejected.why: magnanimitas here means generosity/long-suffering, not magnanimity (greatness of soul).
last_rejected.ruling: Magnanimitas covers magnanimity/generosity; rendering within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: castitas in this Pauline list means sexual purity/continence, not chastity in the broader sense.
last_rejected.ruling: Castitas = chastity/sexual purity; standard rendering, no meaning lost or changed.
